summary: Target-level plan of EDC.7 (pure perverse sheaves, weights and the decomposition theorem) and EDC.8 (cohomological correspondences, trace formulas and the functional-equation interface). EDC.7 follows BBD chapter 5: Frobenius descent of perverse sheaves, mixed perverse sheaves and pointwise weight criteria, Ext-vanishing between weights, the H⁰-on-affines criterion, stability of weights under subquotients and intermediate extension (purity of IC), the weight filtration via the abstract splitting lemma, geometric semisimplicity of pure perverse sheaves, the classification of pure indecomposables and the open–closed decomposition, weights of perverse cohomology, the splitting of pure complexes, the decomposition theorem for proper maps over finite fields and its semismall form, abstract and relative hard Lefschetz with primitive decompositions (via the universal hyperplane section), and BBD chapter 6's passage to ℂ (restricted categories, geometric origin, pure specialisation, decomposition and relative hard Lefschetz over ℂ). Weil II enters only through DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7–DWP.8. EDC.8 follows Varshavsky: correspondences, cohomological correspondences, pushforward, pullback and restriction, composition (Lu–Zheng), trace maps and local terms, compatibility with proper pushforward, the Lefschetz–Verdier formula and its zero-dimensional case, additivity, specialisation and the deformation to the normal cone, contracting correspondences, Frobenius twists, the Fujiwara–Varshavsky trace formula, and true versus naive local terms for semisimple and finite-order automorphisms; and the graded Frobenius duality datum with reciprocity of characteristic polynomials, the middle-degree determinant and Δ² = q^{dχ}, exported to WeilConjectures. Scheme-only: stacks and perfect schemes are recorded as Part II gaps.

conventions: Weights: ι-free integer weights of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8. K has weights ≤ w when ℋ^i(K) has punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w by Verdier duality; geometric Frobenius acts on ℚ̄_ℓ(1) by q^{−1}, so ℚ̄_ℓ(1) has weight −2 and K(r) shifts weights by −2r.
Perverse normalisation: IC_X(L) = j_!*(L[d]) with no Tate half-twist; L lisse punctually pure of weight w gives IC of weight w + d.
Coefficients: ℚ̄_ℓ as the 2-colimit over finite E/ℚ_ℓ of the rational adic categories of EDC.6; finite-field arithmetic objects carry an index 0 (X₀, F₀), their pullbacks to 𝔽̄_q drop it.

Cohomological correspondences: u : c₁^*F₁ → c₂^!F₂ (pull back along the first leg); the graph-type correspondence of g is (g, id), whose c-morphisms are u : g^*F → F; the n-th Frobenius twist is (Fr^n ∘ c₁, c₂).
Duality data for the functional equation: Δ := ∏_i det(F_i)^{(−1)^i}, so Δ² = q^{dχ}, the convention of WeilConjectures:WC.2.

nodes.title: Perverse sheaves over 𝔽_q as Frobenius-equivariant perverse sheaves over 𝔽̄_q
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be separated of finite type over 𝔽_q and K₀, L₀ ∈ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ), with pullbacks K, L to X. (a) For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → Hom^{i−1}(K, L)_F → Hom^i(K₀, L₀) → Hom^i(K, L)^F → 0, where Hom^i := Hom(−, −[i]) in the derived category, F is the geometric Frobenius acting on the finite-dimensional ℚ̄_ℓ-space Hom^i(K, L) = H^i RHom(K, L) by transport of structure, and the subscript/superscript F denote coinvariants/invariants. (b) The functor sending a perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ to the pair (F, φ), φ : Fr*F ≅ F its Weil descent isomorphism, is fully faithful from Perv(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) to the category of perverse sheaves on X equipped with an isomorphism Fr*F ≅ F, and its essential image is stable under extensions and under subquotients. (c) The functor is not essentially surjective: over X₀ = Spec 𝔽_q the pair (ℚ̄_ℓ, multiplication by a non-unit u ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ^×) is not in the image.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
The Frobenius acting on Hom^i(K, L) is the one induced by the descent data of K₀ and L₀; continuous Galois cohomology of Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ is used.
proofSteps: Write Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = H^i RΓ(Spec 𝔽_q, Ra_* RHom(K₀, L₀)) for a : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q, and identify the geometric fibre of Ra_*RHom(K₀, L₀) with RHom(K, L) by proper/smooth base change for RHom of constructible complexes over a field (SF.2 Hochschild–Serre for Galois coverings, passed to adic coefficients).

The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ has only the columns p = 0, 1, since continuous cohomology of ℤ̂ with finite-dimensional ℓ-adic coefficients is invariants in degree 0, coinvariants in degree 1 and zero above; this gives (a) (BBD (5.1.2.3)–(5.1.2.5)).
For perverse K₀, L₀ the group Hom^{−1}(K, L) vanishes (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory), so (a) with i = 0 gives full faithfulness: Hom(K₀, L₀) = Hom(K, L)^F.

With i = 1, Ext¹ in Perv(X₀) and Ext¹ in the category of pairs (F, φ) both sit in exact sequences with Hom(K, L)_F on the left and Ext¹(K, L)^F on the right; equal dimensions and injectivity give a bijection, hence stability under extensions.

Stability under subquotients follows from the noetherian-induction Lemma 5.1.3 of BBD: on a smooth dense open where a sub-object is a shifted lisse sheaf, a Frobenius-stable lisse subquotient descends; extend by p j_!, p j_* and the closed complement.
The non-example over a point: a Weil-descent isomorphism of ℚ̄_ℓ which is multiplication by a non-ℓ-adic unit is not the Frobenius of a continuous ℓ-adic Galois representation.
acceptance: Over X₀ = Spec 𝔽_q, K₀ = L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ: Hom^0 = ℚ̄_ℓ and Hom^1(K₀, L₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ (coinvariants of the trivial action), while Hom^1(K, L) = 0.
For K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ and L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ(1) on Spec 𝔽_q: F acts on Hom(K, L) = ℚ̄_ℓ by q^{-1} ≠ 1, so invariants and coinvariants vanish and Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for all i.

nodes.title: Mixed perverse sheaves and the perverse t-structure on mixed complexes
nodes.statement: For X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q, let D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) ⊂ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) be the full triangulated subcategory of mixed complexes (DWP.8/mixed-complexes). The middle perverse t-structure of D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) restricts to a t-structure on D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ); its heart Perv_m(X₀) is the category of mixed perverse sheaves: perverse sheaves on X₀ whose ordinary cohomology sheaves are mixed. Perv_m(X₀) is a full abelian subcategory of Perv(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) stable under kernels, cokernels, extensions and all subquotients. A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w, pure of weight w) when F₀ ∈ D^b_m has; with the shifted convention of DWP.8, F₀[1] has weights ≤ w + 1 exactly when F₀ has weights ≤ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Mixedness is tested on ordinary cohomology sheaves; perverse truncations are computed in D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ).
proofSteps: D^b_m(X₀) is stable under f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, Rf^!, ⊗, RHom and Verdier duality (DWP.8/six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11) and under the ordinary truncations, since mixedness is a condition on cohomology sheaves (BBD 5.1.6).

The perverse truncations are built from these operations along a stratification (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure, gluing), so they preserve D^b_m; hence the perverse t-structure restricts (BBD 5.1.7(i)).
The heart of the restricted t-structure is a full subcategory of Perv(X₀) stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions (it is the intersection with a triangulated subcategory).

Stability under subquotients: apply BBD Lemma 5.1.3/Remark 5.1.4 to the system of subcategories Perv_m(Y₀) for all subschemes Y₀, whose hypotheses (stability under p j_!, p j_*, closed pushforward, lisse subquotients on smooth strata) hold by DWP.8 stability (BBD 5.1.7(ii)).
acceptance: ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth pure d-dimensional X₀ is mixed perverse and pure of weight d.
On Spec 𝔽_q, Perv_m is the category of finite-dimensional continuous ℚ̄_ℓ-representations of Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) whose Frobenius eigenvalues are q-Weil numbers of integer weight.

nodes.title: Weights are tested at closed points and are insensitive to finite extension of 𝔽_q
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ). (a) K₀ has weights ≤ w iff i_x^*K₀ has weights ≤ w for every closed point i_x : x → X₀; K₀ has weights ≥ w iff i_x^!K₀ has weights ≥ w for every closed point x. (b) For n ≥ 1, the pullback K₁ of K₀ to X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{qⁿ} is mixed (resp. of weights ≤ w, ≥ w) iff K₀ is; hence weights of an object over 𝔽̄_q are defined once it descends to some 𝔽_{qⁿ}. (c) Weights are additive under external products: inf{w : K₀ ⊠ L₀ ∈ D_{≤w}} = inf{w : K₀ ∈ D_{≤w}} + inf{w : L₀ ∈ D_{≤w}}, and dually for the lower bounds.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
In (c), X₀ × Y₀ is the fibre product over 𝔽_q and K₀ ⊠ L₀ := pr₁^*K₀ ⊗ pr₂^*L₀.
proofSteps: (a), first half: weights ≤ w are defined by the punctual weights of ℋ^i, i.e. by the stalks at closed points, which are the cohomology of i_x^*K₀.
(a), second half: K₀ has weights ≥ w iff D K₀ has weights ≤ −w; apply the first half to D K₀ and use i_x^* D = D i_x^! (EDC.1:biduality/duality-exchange-isomorphisms).

(b): the closed points of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{qⁿ} lie over those of X₀ and the Frobenius of the residue field of a point over x is a power of that of x; Weil q^{deg}-numbers of weight w are preserved and detected by powers.

(c): the upper bound ≤ w + w′ is stability of ⊗ and pullback (DWP.8/directional-weight-estimates); equality is checked at closed points (a), where the stalk of K₀ ⊠ L₀ at (x, y) is the tensor product of the stalks and eigenvalue weights add; the lower bound follows by duality since ⊠ commutes with Verdier duality (EDC.1:biduality, Künneth for dualizing complexes).
acceptance: ℚ̄_ℓ on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} is pure of weight 0: at every closed point x, i_x^*ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 and i_x^!ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−2] has weight 2 − 2 = 0; its perverse shift ℚ̄_ℓ[1] is pure of weight 1.
ℚ̄_ℓ(1) ⊠ ℚ̄_ℓ(1) on Spec 𝔽_q is ℚ̄_ℓ(2), of weight −4 = (−2) + (−2).

nodes.title: Ext-vanishing between weights
nodes.statement: Let K₀, L₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) and w ∈ ℤ. (a) If K₀ has weights ≤ w and L₀ has weights > w (i.e. ≥ w + 1), then Ra_*RHom(K₀, L₀) ∈ D_{>0}(Spec 𝔽_q) for a : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q, and Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) = 0 for all i > 0. (b) If K₀ has weights ≤ w and L₀ has weights ≥ w, then F has no invariants on Hom(K, L[i]) for i > 0, so the restriction Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) → Hom(K, L[i]) is zero for i > 0, and Hom(K₀, L₀[i]) = 0 for i ≥ 2. (c) In particular, for mixed perverse K₀ of weights ≤ w and L₀ of weights > w: Hom(K₀, L₀) = 0 and Ext¹_{Perv(X₀)}(K₀, L₀) = 0; for simple mixed perverse U₀, V₀ pure of weights u > v, Ext¹(V₀, U₀) = 0.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: RHom(K₀, L₀) has weights ≥ (w+1) − w = 1 by DWP.8/directional-weight-estimates (v), and Ra_* preserves lower bounds (ii); so Ra_*RHom ∈ D_{≥1} = D_{>0}, giving (a) first part (BBD 5.1.15(i)).
On Spec 𝔽_q, a complex of weights > 0 has H^i of weights > i ≥ 0 for i ≥ 0, so Frobenius has no eigenvalue 1: invariants and coinvariants of Hom^i(K, L) vanish for i ≥ 0.
Insert into the exact sequences of EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves: Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for i > 0, which is (a) (BBD 5.1.15(ii)).
With weights ≥ w for L₀, Hom^i(K, L) has weights ≥ i, hence > 0 for i ≥ 1: invariants vanish for i > 0 and coinvariants vanish for i ≥ 1, giving (b) (BBD 5.1.15(iii)).
(c): for perverse K₀, L₀, Hom^0 = Hom(K, L)^F with weights > 0 has no invariants; Ext¹ in Perv is Hom^1 (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory). The simple pure case is the instance used in BBD 5.3.5.
acceptance: K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ, L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) on Spec 𝔽_q (weights 0 and 2): Hom^i(K₀, L₀) = 0 for all i, since Frobenius acts by q ≠ 1.
Sharpness of the strict inequality: K₀ = L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ on Spec 𝔽_q (both of weight 0) has Ext¹(K₀, L₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ ≠ 0, realised by the unipotent rank-two sheaf E₂.

nodes.title: Lower weights of a mixed perverse sheaf are detected by H⁰ on affine étale opens
nodes.statement: A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has weights ≥ w iff for every affine étale map u : U₀ → X₀ the Frobenius module H⁰(U, u^*F) (hypercohomology of the pullback over 𝔽̄_q, with U₀ defined over a finite extension 𝔽_{qⁿ} as allowed by EDC.7/pointwise-weight-criteria (b)) has weights ≥ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
U₀ → X₀ étale with U₀ affine; H⁰ is hypercohomology of the complex u^*F over 𝔽̄_q.
proofSteps: Necessity: u^! = u^* for étale u preserves weights ≥ w, and RΓ = Ra_* preserves lower bounds (DWP.8/directional-weight-estimates (ii)); H⁰ of a complex of weights ≥ w has weights ≥ w.

Sufficiency on a smooth connected curve (BBD 5.2.2): filter F₀ by simple perverse constituents, which are (j_*L₀)[1] = j_!*(L₀[1]) for irreducible lisse L₀ or punctual; both are pure; count dimensions of H^{−1} and H⁰ on affine opens with many points over a closed point to exclude constituents of small weight.

General case (BBD 5.2.3–5.2.8): by restriction to curves through general points and noetherian induction, using the largest perverse subsheaf with punctual support and its weight, and the exact sequences of perverse cohomology on affine opens (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing).
The weights of H⁰(U, F) are those of the Frobenius of 𝔽_{qⁿ} acting by transport of structure (BBD 5.1.11–5.1.12).
acceptance: F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔾_{m,𝔽_q}: H⁰(𝔾_m, ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) = H¹(𝔾_m, ℚ̄_ℓ) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 ≥ 1, consistent with weights ≥ 1, while H^{−1} = H⁰(𝔾_m) has weight 0 < 1 and is not tested.
A punctual perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ(1) at a rational point has H⁰ = ℚ̄_ℓ(1) of weight −2 on every affine étale neighbourhood, so it does not have weights ≥ −1.

sources.match: BBD characterise lower weights of a mixed perverse sheaf by the weights of H⁰(U, F) on affine étale U, first on smooth curves and then in general.

nodes.title: Subquotients of mixed perverse sheaves keep their weight bounds
nodes.statement: If a mixed perverse sheaf F₀ has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w), every subquotient of F₀ in Perv(X₀) has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: (a), quotients: reduce to w = 0 by twist; for a quotient G₀ of F₀ and affine étale U, H⁰(U, G) is a quotient of H⁰(U, F) (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing gives H¹ of perverse sheaves on affines zero), so has weights ≥ 0, and EDC.7/affine-cohomology-weight-criterion applies.

(a), subobjects: the sequence H^{−1}(U, F/G) → H⁰(U, G) → H⁰(U, F) gives weights ≥ −1 for G; pass to G ⊠ G ⊂ F ⊠ F on X₀ × X₀ and use additivity (EDC.7/pointwise-weight-criteria (c)) to get weights ≥ −1/2, hence ≥ 0 since weights are integers. The upper bounds follow by duality (BBD 5.3.1).
acceptance: On Spec 𝔽_q the unipotent rank-two sheaf E₂ (Frobenius a single Jordan block with eigenvalue 1) is pure of weight 0, and its unique rank-one subobject and quotient ℚ̄_ℓ are pure of weight 0.
On Spec 𝔽_q, ℚ̄_ℓ ⊕ ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weights ≤ 2 and ≥ 0; its quotient ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 ≤ 2 and its subobject ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 ≥ 0, while neither bound can be improved for the sum.

sources.match: BBD show that subquotients of a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≥ w (≤ w) keep the bound, via H⁰ on affines, the external-square trick and integrality of weights, and obtain the upper bound by duality.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension along an affine immersion preserves weights; purity of IC
nodes.statement: (a) Let j : U₀ ↪ X₀ be an affine locally closed immersion and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf on U₀. If F₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w), so does j_!*F₀; if F₀ is pure of weight w, j_!*F₀ is pure of weight w. (b) Let X₀ be irreducible of dimension d, U₀ ⊂ X₀ a dense open subscheme smooth over 𝔽_q and L₀ a lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ punctually pure of weight w. Then the intersection complex IC_{X₀}(L₀) = j_!*(L₀[d]) of EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system is a pure perverse sheaf of weight w + d; in particular IC_{X₀} := IC_{X₀}(ℚ̄_ℓ) is pure of weight d. (c) Consequently, for X₀ proper over 𝔽_q, the intersection cohomology H^i(X, IC_X(L)) is pure of weight w + d + i for every i.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
(a): j affine (j_! and Rj_* are then t-exact for the perverse t-structure). (b): the shift is the perverse normalisation L₀[d]; no Tate half-twist is built in.
proofSteps: (a) Since j is affine and quasi-finite, j_!F₀ and Rj_*F₀ are perverse (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing, BBD 4.1.3).

If F₀ has weights ≤ w, j_!F₀ has weights ≤ w (DWP.8/directional-weight-estimates (i)); j_!*F₀ is the image of j_!F₀ → Rj_*F₀, a quotient of j_!F₀ in Perv(X₀), so it has weights ≤ w by EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability.
Dually, if F₀ has weights ≥ w, Rj_*F₀ has weights ≥ w and its subobject j_!*F₀ has weights ≥ w; combining both gives purity (BBD 5.3.2, first proof).

(b) L₀[d] is pure of weight w + d on the smooth U₀ (DWP.8/twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (c)) and perverse (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse). Shrink U₀ to an affine dense open (IC is independent of the dense open, EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system); a morphism from an affine scheme to the separated X₀ is affine, so U₀ ↪ X₀ is an affine immersion; apply (a).
(c) Proper pushforward to Spec 𝔽_q preserves purity (DWP.8/proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6): RΓ(X, IC) is pure of weight w + d, so H^i is pure of weight w + d + i.
acceptance: For a smooth projective curve C₀ and L₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ: IC = ℚ̄_ℓ[1], pure of weight 1, and H^i(C, ℚ̄_ℓ[1]) = H^{i+1}(C, ℚ̄_ℓ) is pure of weight i + 1.

For the nodal cubic X₀ with normalisation ν : ℙ¹ → X₀ (ν finite birational), IC_{X₀} = ν_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1], so IH^0(X) = H¹(ℙ¹) = 0 although H¹(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0: the constant sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on X₀ is not pure of weight 1.
The specialisation X₀ smooth projective of dimension d gives IC = ℚ̄_ℓ[d] and recovers purity of H^i(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) of weight i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7, Weil II 3.3.9).

sources.locator: Corollaire 5.3.2 with its first proof, p. 135
sources.match: BBD prove that for an affine immersion j the intermediate extension of a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≤ w (≥ w) keeps the bound, so pure goes to pure of the same weight, via perversity of j_! and the quotient j_!F → j_!*F.
Shifted lisse pure sheaves on smooth schemes are pure, and proper direct images preserve purity.

nodes.title: Simple mixed perverse sheaves are pure
nodes.statement: Every simple object of Perv_m(X₀) is pure: it is isomorphic to i_*j_!*(L₀[d]) for i the closure of a smooth connected locally closed U₀ ⊂ X₀ of dimension d, j : U₀ ↪ Ū₀ open and L₀ an irreducible lisse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ punctually pure of some integer weight β, and it is pure of weight β + d.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: A simple mixed perverse sheaf is simple in Perv(X₀) (EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves: subobjects of mixed are mixed), so it is i_*j_!*(L₀[d]) with L₀ irreducible lisse on a smooth connected U₀ (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification, applied to arithmetic objects through EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves).

Shrink U₀ (allowed, EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system): L₀ is mixed and irreducible, so its weight filtration by lisse subsheaves (DWP.7/weights-mixed-sheaves-definitions; Weil II 3.4.1(ii)) has a single step and L₀ is punctually pure.
Take U₀ affine and apply EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity (BBD 5.3.4).
acceptance: The punctual simple perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ(r) at a closed point is pure of weight −2r.
On Spec 𝔽_q a simple mixed perverse sheaf is a one-dimensional continuous ℚ̄_ℓ-representation whose Frobenius eigenvalue is a q-Weil number of some integer weight β, and it is pure of weight β.

sources.match: BBD: every simple mixed perverse sheaf is pure, by writing it as an intermediate extension of an irreducible, hence pure, lisse sheaf on an affine smooth open.

nodes.title: Splitting lemma for a partition of simple objects with Ext¹-vanishing
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian category in which every object has finite length. Let S⁺ ⊔ S⁻ be a partition of the isomorphism classes of simple objects, and A⁺ (resp. A⁻) the full subcategory of objects all of whose simple subquotients lie in S⁺ (resp. S⁻). Assume every short exact sequence 0 → U → E → V → 0 with U ∈ S⁺ and V ∈ S⁻ splits. Then every object F has a unique subobject W F ∈ A⁻ with F / W F ∈ A⁺; Hom(A⁺, A⁻) = Hom(A⁻, A⁺) = 0 and Ext¹(A⁻, A⁺) = 0; and every morphism f : F → G satisfies f(W F) = f(F) ∩ W G.
hypotheses: A abelian, every object of finite length (artinian and noetherian); the partition is of isomorphism classes of simple objects; Ext¹ vanishing is only required from S⁻ to S⁺.
proofSteps: Ext¹(Y, X) = 0 for X ∈ A⁺, Y ∈ A⁻ by dévissage along composition series and the long exact Ext sequence; Hom vanishings because A⁺ and A⁻ share no simple constituents.

Existence by induction on length: choose a simple subobject S ⊂ F and W(F/S); its preimage E is an extension of W(F/S) by S. If S ∈ S⁻ take W F = E; if S ∈ S⁺ the extension splits by Ext¹(W(F/S), S) = 0, take a lift of W(F/S).
Uniqueness: for two candidates W′, W″ the composites W′ → F → F/W″ and W″ → F → F/W′ vanish by Hom(A⁻, A⁺) = 0.
Strictness: both f(W F) and f(F) ∩ W G have the characteristic property of W(f(F)).
acceptance: A = finite-dimensional representations of ℤ over ℚ̄_ℓ on which the generator acts with eigenvalues in {1, q}, S⁻ = {eigenvalue 1}, S⁺ = {eigenvalue q}: W F is the generalized 1-eigenspace and the splitting is the generalized eigenspace decomposition.

Without the Ext¹ hypothesis the conclusion fails: for finite-dimensional representations of the quiver 1 → 2 over a field, the indecomposable projective P₁ is a non-split extension of S₁ by S₂; with S⁻ = {S₁} and S⁺ = {S₂}, its subobjects are 0, S₂ and P₁, and none lies in A⁻ with quotient in A⁺.

sources.match: BBD's abstract lemma: in a finite-length abelian category with a partition of simples and vanishing Ext¹ from the second class to the first, each object has a unique subobject in A⁻ with quotient in A⁺, functorial and strict.

nodes.title: The weight filtration of a mixed perverse sheaf

planet.name: Weight filtration of mixed perverse sheaves

nodes.statement: Every mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has a unique finite increasing filtration W = (W_i F₀)_{i ∈ ℤ} by perverse subsheaves, with W_i F₀ = 0 for i ≪ 0 and W_i F₀ = F₀ for i ≫ 0, such that Gr^W_i F₀ := W_i F₀ / W_{i−1} F₀ is pure of weight i for every i. W_i F₀ is the largest perverse subsheaf of weights ≤ i, and F₀ / W_i F₀ has weights > i. Every morphism f : F₀ → G₀ of mixed perverse sheaves is strictly compatible: f(W_i F₀) = f(F₀) ∩ W_i G₀. The filtration is an arithmetic object on X₀; after base change to 𝔽̄_q it need not split Frobenius-equivariantly, although each graded piece becomes semisimple (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Weights are integers (mixed in the sense of DWP.7, not ι-mixed with real weights); for ι-mixed objects BBD 5.3.5 applies to the weight-class decomposition modulo ℤ first.
proofSteps: Perv_m(X₀) is abelian with all objects of finite length (EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves, EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification), and simple objects are pure (EDC.7/simple-mixed-perverse-is-pure).
For each i, partition the simple classes into S⁺ (weight > i) and S⁻ (weight ≤ i); Ext¹(V, U) = 0 for U ∈ S⁺, V ∈ S⁻ by EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (c).
EDC.7/torsion-theory-splitting-lemma gives the unique W_i F₀ with constituents of weight ≤ i and quotient with constituents of weight > i, and strictness.

An object of A⁻ has weights ≤ i (weights ≤ i are stable under extensions, DWP.8/mixed-complexes) and conversely constituents of an object of weights ≤ i have weights ≤ i (EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability); so W_i F₀ is the largest subobject of weights ≤ i and Gr^W_i is pure of weight i (BBD 5.3.5).
acceptance: For F₀ pure of weight w: W_{w−1}F₀ = 0 and W_w F₀ = F₀.

On 𝔾_{m,𝔽_q} with j : 𝔾_m ↪ 𝔸¹, the perverse sheaf Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] sits in 0 → ℚ̄_ℓ,𝔸¹[1] → Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] → δ₀(−1) → 0; its weight filtration has Gr_1 = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] and Gr_2 = δ₀(−1), the punctual sheaf at 0 of weight 2.

nodes.title: Upper weights of a mixed perverse sheaf are detected generically on closed subvarieties
nodes.statement: A mixed perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ has weights ≤ w iff every irreducible closed subscheme Y₀ ⊆ X₀, of dimension d, has a dense open U₀ ⊆ Y₀ on which the ordinary cohomology sheaf ℋ^{−d}(F₀)|_{U₀} has punctual weights ≤ w − d.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: Necessity: weights ≤ w means ℋ^{−d} has punctual weights ≤ w − d everywhere.

Sufficiency: otherwise, by EDC.7/weight-filtration, F₀ has a simple quotient G₀ pure of weight w′ > w, of the form j_!*(L₀[d]) on a smooth affine connected U₀ ⊂ Y₀ with L₀ punctually pure of weight w′ − d (EDC.7/simple-mixed-perverse-is-pure).

The long exact cohomology sequence of 0 → Ker → F₀ → G₀ → 0 gives, on a dense open of Y₀, a surjection ℋ^{−d}(F₀) → ℋ^{−d}(G₀) = L₀ (degree −d is the top degree there by the perverse stalk bounds, EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure); so L₀ has weights ≤ w − d, contradicting w′ > w (BBD 5.3.7).
acceptance: For F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] ⊕ δ₀(−1) on 𝔸¹: on Y₀ = 𝔸¹ the generic sheaf ℋ^{−1} = ℚ̄_ℓ has weight 0 ≤ w − 1 iff w ≥ 1, and on Y₀ = {0} the sheaf ℋ^0 contains ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) of weight 2 ≤ w iff w ≥ 2; so F₀ has weights ≤ 2 and not ≤ 1.

sources.match: BBD: a mixed perverse sheaf has weights ≤ w iff on a dense open of each irreducible d-dimensional closed subvariety the cohomology sheaf in degree −d has punctual weights ≤ w − d.

nodes.title: Semisimple and geometrically semisimple perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: An object of an abelian category is semisimple if it is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of simple objects. A perverse sheaf F on X (over 𝔽̄_q) is semisimple if it is semisimple in Perv(X, ℚ̄_ℓ); then F ≅ ⊕_k i_{V_k*} j_{k!*}(L_k[d_k]) with V_k smooth connected locally closed of dimension d_k and L_k irreducible lisse. A perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀ is geometrically semisimple if its pullback F to X is semisimple; a complex K₀ ∈ D^b_c(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) is geometrically split-semisimple if its pullback K satisfies K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] with every pH^i(K) semisimple. No condition on the Frobenius structure is imposed.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Semisimplicity is a property of the geometric object over 𝔽̄_q, not of F₀ in Perv(X₀); a decomposition of K is an isomorphism, not a canonical one.
proofSteps: Finite direct sums exist in Perv(X) (an additive heart); finite length makes 'sum of simple subobjects' and 'finite direct sum of simples' agree.
The description of simple objects is EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification.

For lisse sheaves on a smooth connected X₀ shifted by dim X₀, the definition agrees with geometric semisimplicity of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/geometric-semisimplicity, since L ↦ L[d] is an exact fully faithful embedding of lisse sheaves into Perv(X) whose essential image is closed under subquotients on smooth X.
acceptance: The constant sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth connected X₀ is geometrically semisimple (it is simple over 𝔽̄_q).
The arithmetic sheaf E₂ (unipotent Frobenius) on Spec 𝔽_q is geometrically semisimple (over 𝔽̄_q it is ℚ̄_ℓ²) but not semisimple in Perv(Spec 𝔽_q).

uses.how: the conclusion of the decomposition theorem is geometric split-semisimplicity
semisimplicity of the Satake category over 𝔽̄_q, used to show the Tannakian group is reductive
the Hitchin direct image over the elliptic locus is a direct sum of shifted simple perverse sheaves whose supports are then studied
endomorphisms of a middle-extension direct image are determined on a dense open

api.name: TauCeti.EtaleDuality.IsSemisimpleObject.of_mono

nodes.title: Pure perverse sheaves are geometrically semisimple

planet.name: Geometric semisimplicity of pure perverse sheaves

nodes.statement: If F₀ is a pure perverse sheaf on X₀ (of some weight w), then F₀ is geometrically semisimple: over 𝔽̄_q, F is a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves i_*j_!*(L[d]) with L irreducible lisse on smooth connected U ⊂ X of dimension d. Neither F₀ in Perv(X₀) nor the Frobenius action is asserted semisimple.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Purity of the arithmetic object F₀ is the hypothesis; a perverse sheaf over 𝔽̄_q with no pure model is not covered.
proofSteps: Let F′ ⊆ F be the socle (sum of simple perverse subsheaves); it is Frobenius-stable, so it descends to F′₀ ⊆ F₀ (EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves, stability under subquotients).
F′₀ and F″₀ := F₀ / F′₀ are pure of weight w (EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability).
The class of 0 → F′₀ → F₀ → F″₀ → 0 in Hom^1(F″₀, F′₀) maps to zero in Hom^1(F″, F′) (EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (b)), so F ≅ F′ ⊕ F″ over 𝔽̄_q.
If F″ ≠ 0 it has a simple subobject, which lifts to a simple subobject of F not in F′, contradicting maximality; so F = F′ is semisimple (BBD 5.3.8, copying Weil II 3.4.1(iii)).
acceptance: DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/geometric-semisimplicity-theorem-3-4-1-iii (a punctually pure lisse sheaf on a normal X₀ is geometrically semisimple) is recovered for smooth connected X₀ by applying the theorem to L₀[dim X₀].
E₂ on Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and geometrically semisimple, but F₀ = E₂ is not semisimple: the theorem asserts nothing about the arithmetic category.

sources.match: BBD prove that a pure perverse sheaf becomes a direct sum of simple perverse sheaves over 𝔽̄_q, by descending the socle and killing the extension class with 5.1.15(iii).
The lisse case on a normal base, whose proof BBD copy.

nodes.title: Indecomposable pure perverse sheaves are Jordan blocks on simple ones
nodes.statement: (a) The indecomposable pure perverse sheaves on X₀ with ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients are exactly S₀ ⊗ E_n with S₀ simple and n ≥ 1, where E_n is the pullback to X₀ of the rank-n sheaf on Spec 𝔽_q on which geometric Frobenius acts unipotently with one Jordan block. (b) If S₀ is simple, there are d ≥ 1 and a perverse sheaf S₁ on X₁ := X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{q^d} such that S₀ ≅ π_*S₁ for π : X₁ → X₀, S₁ is geometrically simple (its pullback to X is simple) and S₁ is not isomorphic to any of its conjugates under Gal(𝔽_{q^d}/𝔽_q). Part (a) also holds with coefficients a finite E/ℚ_ℓ; part (b) does not in general.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
proofSteps: For F₀ with F semisimple (e.g. F₀ pure, EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity), decompose F into isotypic components indexed by isomorphism classes a of simple constituents; Frobenius permutes the classes, and orbits C give a decomposition F₀ = ⊕_C F₀,C descending by EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves.
For an orbit of length d, the a-part is defined over 𝔽_{q^d} and F₀,C ≅ π_*(F₁,a); choose φ : Fr^{d*}G_a ≅ G_a for a simple G_a; then F₁,a ≅ G_a ⊗ V_a with V_a := Hom(G_a, F_a) carrying a Frobenius.

Indecomposability forces one orbit and a single Jordan block on V_a; rescaling φ makes it unipotent, giving S₀ ⊗ E_n with S₀ = π_*(G₁) simple (BBD 5.3.9(i)); for F₀ simple, V_a is one-dimensional, giving (b).

With E coefficients the linear algebra of 5.3.9(i) still goes through, but the descent of a geometrically simple constituent to a finite extension may need a coefficient extension, so (b) fails as stated (BBD 5.3.10).
acceptance: E_n on Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and indecomposable but not simple for n ≥ 2.

Let X₀ = Spec 𝔽_{q²}, viewed over 𝔽_q: the simple perverse sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ on X₀ pulls back to ℚ̄_ℓ ⊕ ℚ̄_ℓ on the two geometric points, so it is not geometrically simple; it is π_*S₁ for d = 2 and S₁ the constant sheaf on one of the two components of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽_{q²}, which is geometrically simple and not isomorphic to its Galois conjugate.

sources.match: BBD classify indecomposable pure perverse sheaves as tensor products of simple ones with unipotent Jordan blocks, describe simple ones by induction from a finite extension, and note what survives with E_λ coefficients.

nodes.title: A pure perverse sheaf splits into an intermediate extension and a part supported on the complement
nodes.statement: Let F₀ be a pure perverse sheaf on X₀, j : U₀ ↪ X₀ open and i : Z₀ ↪ X₀ the complementary closed immersion. Then F₀ has a unique decomposition F₀ = j_!*F′₀ ⊕ i_*F″₀ in Perv(X₀), with F′₀ = j^*F₀; the adjunction map pj_!j^*F₀ → F₀ factors through the quotient j_!*j^*F₀ of pj_!j^*F₀, the map F₀ → pj_*j^*F₀ through the subobject j_!*j^*F₀ of pj_*j^*F₀, and the composite of adjunction maps i_* pH⁰(i^!F₀) → F₀ → i_* pH⁰(i^*F₀) is an isomorphism (both sides equal i_*F″₀).
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
F₀ pure; for mixed F₀ the decomposition fails (e.g. Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔸¹).
proofSteps: Uniqueness: Hom(j_!*F′, i_*F″) = Hom(i_*F″, j_!*F′) = 0 since j_!* has no subobject or quotient supported on Z (EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension).
By EDC.7/frobenius-descent-of-perverse-sheaves it suffices to check the factorisations and that the maps are the inclusions and projections of a decomposition over 𝔽̄_q.

Over 𝔽̄_q, F is semisimple (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity), so it suffices to treat its simple constituents, each of the form j_!*G′ or i_*G″ (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification), for which the statements are immediate (BBD 5.3.11).
acceptance: For the mixed, not pure, perverse sheaf F₀ = Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[1] on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} with Z = {0}: i^!F₀ = 0 while pH⁰(i^*F₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) ≠ 0, so the composite in the statement is not an isomorphism, and F₀ is a non-split extension of δ₀(−1) by ℚ̄_ℓ[1]; purity is necessary.
For F₀ = IC_{X₀} with X₀ irreducible and U₀ dense, F″₀ = 0.

sources.locator: Corollaire 5.3.11, p. 140 (checked on the page image)
sources.match: BBD: a pure perverse sheaf has a unique decomposition j_!*F′ ⊕ i_*F″, with the adjunction maps factoring through the intermediate extension and i_*pi^!F → F → i_*pi^*F an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Weights of a mixed complex are read off its perverse cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ). (a) K₀ has weights ≤ w (resp. ≥ w) iff every perverse cohomology sheaf pH^i(K₀) has weights ≤ w + i (resp. ≥ w + i). (b) K₀ is pure of weight w iff every pH^i(K₀) is pure of weight w + i. (c) For f : X₀ → Y₀ of finite type and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf of weights ≤ w, the perverse sheaves pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) and pH⁰(f^*F₀) have weights ≤ w; if F₀ has weights ≥ w, pH⁰(Rf_*F₀) and pH⁰(Rf^!F₀) have weights ≥ w.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Perverse truncation and perverse cohomology are those of EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves; the shift convention puts pH^i(K₀)[−i] in weights ≤ w + i − i = w when pH^i has weights ≤ w + i.
proofSteps: Sufficiency in (a): weights ≤ w are stable under extensions in triangles (DWP.8/mixed-complexes); use the triangles (pτ_{<i}K₀, pτ_{≤i}K₀, pH^i(K₀)[−i]).

Necessity in (a), by descending induction on i, reduced to w = 0 and showing pH⁰K₀ ≤ 0 once pH^i K₀ ≤ i for i > 0: then pτ_{>0}K₀ ≤ 0, so pτ_{≤0}K₀ ≤ 0 by the triangle; the sequence ℋ^{−d}(pτ_{<0}K₀) → ℋ^{−d}(pH⁰K₀) → ℋ^{−d+1}(pτ_{<0}K₀) and the vanishing of the outer terms generically on each d-dimensional irreducible Y₀ give generic punctual weights ≤ −d; conclude by EDC.7/generic-weight-criterion (BBD 5.4.1). The lower-bound statement is dual.
(b) is (a) applied to both bounds (BBD 5.4.4).
(c): Rf_!, f^* preserve upper bounds and Rf_*, f^! lower bounds (DWP.8/directional-weight-estimates); apply (a) to the degree-0 perverse cohomology (BBD 5.4.2).
acceptance: For X₀ smooth of dimension d, K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ (weight 0): pH^d(K₀) = ℚ̄_ℓ[d] is pure of weight 0 + d, and all other pH^i vanish.

For f : 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q} → Spec 𝔽_q and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1] (pure of weight 1): Rf_!F₀ = H²_c(𝔸¹)[−1] = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−1], whose only perverse cohomology sheaf pH¹ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1) has weight 2 = 1 + 1; by (b), Rf_!F₀ is pure of weight 1.

sources.match: BBD: K₀ has weights ≤ w (≥ w) iff each pH^iK₀ has weights ≤ w + i (≥ w + i); hence perverse cohomology of a pure complex is pure, and pH⁰ of f_!, f^* (f_*, f^!) preserve upper (lower) weight bounds.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension along a quasi-finite morphism preserves weights
nodes.statement: Let f : X₀ → Y₀ be quasi-finite (for example any locally closed immersion) and F₀ a mixed perverse sheaf on X₀. Define f_!*F₀ := Im(pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) → pH⁰(Rf_*F₀)). If F₀ has weights ≥ w (resp. ≤ w), so does f_!*F₀; pure perverse sheaves go to pure perverse sheaves of the same weight. For a locally closed immersion j this is the intermediate extension j_!* of EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension, without the affineness hypothesis of EDC.7/intersection-complex-purity.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
f quasi-finite and separated of finite type.
proofSteps: pH⁰(Rf_!F₀) has weights ≤ w when F₀ does and pH⁰(Rf_*F₀) has weights ≥ w when F₀ does (EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights (c)).
f_!*F₀ is a quotient of the first and a subobject of the second, so EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability gives both bounds (BBD 5.4.3, following the first proof of 5.3.2).
For an immersion, the image of pH⁰j_! → pH⁰j_* is j_!* (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension, BBD 1.4.22).
acceptance: For j : 𝔸² ∖ {0} ↪ 𝔸² (quasi-finite, not affine), Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[2] is not perverse (it has the cohomology sheaf δ₀(−2) in degree 1), but the image of pH⁰(Rj_!ℚ̄_ℓ[2]) → pH⁰(Rj_*ℚ̄_ℓ[2]) is j_!*ℚ̄_ℓ[2] = ℚ̄_ℓ[2], pure of weight 2.
For f finite (e.g. a normalisation), f_!* = f_* is exact and preserves purity.

sources.match: BBD: for quasi-finite f, f_!* = Im(pf_! → pf_*) carries perverse sheaves of weights ≥ w (≤ w) to perverse sheaves of weights ≥ w (≤ w), hence pure to pure of the same weight.

nodes.title: Pure complexes split geometrically into shifted intersection complexes
nodes.statement: Let K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) be pure of weight w. Then over 𝔽̄_q: (a) K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] (a finite sum, isomorphism in D^b_c(X, ℚ̄_ℓ)); (b) each pH^i(K) is semisimple, being the pullback of the pure perverse sheaf pH^i(K₀) of weight w + i; (c) consequently K ≅ ⊕_k (i_{V_k*} j_{k!*}(L_k[d_k]))[n_k] for finitely many smooth connected locally closed V_k of dimension d_k, irreducible lisse L_k on V_k and integers n_k. The isomorphism in (a) is not canonical and need not be compatible with the Frobenius structure of K₀.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
Purity of the arithmetic complex K₀ is required; the conclusion is over 𝔽̄_q only.
proofSteps: pH^i(K₀) is pure of weight w + i (EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights (b)), so pH^i(K₀)[−i] is pure of weight w and pτ_{<i}K₀ has weights ≤ w, pH^i(K₀)[−i] weights ≥ w.

The connecting morphism of (pτ_{<i}K₀, pτ_{≤i}K₀, pH^i(K₀)[−i]) is a degree-one map from pH^i(K₀)[−i] to pτ_{<i}K₀; by EDC.7/weight-ext-vanishing (b) its image over 𝔽̄_q is zero, so pτ_{≤i}K ≅ pτ_{<i}K ⊕ pH^i(K)[−i]; induct on i (BBD 5.4.5).
(b) is EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity; (c) combines (a), (b) and the classification of simple perverse sheaves (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification) (BBD 5.4.6).
acceptance: For X₀ smooth projective, K₀ = Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ for f : X₀ → Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0 and the splitting is H*(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ ⊕_i H^i(X)[−i], the elementary decomposition of a complex of vector spaces.
The split is not Frobenius-equivariant in general: E₂[0] on Spec 𝔽_q is pure of weight 0, and its geometric splitting as ℚ̄_ℓ ⊕ ℚ̄_ℓ does not descend to 𝔽_q.

sources.match: BBD: a pure complex over 𝔽_q splits over 𝔽̄_q as the sum of its shifted perverse cohomology sheaves (by 5.4.4 and 5.1.15(iii)), hence as a sum of shifted j_!*L[d] with L irreducible lisse.

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem for proper morphisms over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ be a proper morphism of separated schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q and K₀ ∈ D^b_m(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) pure of weight w (for example K₀ = IC_{X₀}(L₀) with L₀ lisse punctually pure of weight w − dim X₀ on a smooth dense open, or K₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[dim X₀] for X₀ smooth). Then: (a) Rf₀_*K₀ is pure of weight w and each pH^i(Rf₀_*K₀) is pure of weight w + i; (b) over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i]; (c) each pH^i(Rf_*K) is semisimple, a finite sum of i_{V*}j_!*(L[dim V]) with L irreducible lisse on smooth connected V ⊂ Y; (d) for Y₀ proper over 𝔽_q, H^j(Y, Rf_*K) = H^j(X, K) is pure of weight w + j. No integral or mod-ℓ decomposition, no canonical or Frobenius-compatible splitting, and no semisimplicity of the arithmetic Frobenius is asserted.

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem for semismall maps
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be smooth over 𝔽_q of pure dimension n, f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ proper and surjective, and assume f is semismall: dim(X ×_Y X) ≤ n. Choose a stratification of Y₀ into smooth connected locally closed strata S₀ (defined over 𝔽_q after a finite extension) such that each R^q f_*ℚ̄_ℓ restricted to each stratum is lisse; put d_S := dim f^{−1}(y) for y ∈ S, and call S relevant if dim S + 2 d_S = n. Then Rf₀_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] is a pure perverse sheaf of weight n, and over 𝔽̄_q there is an isomorphism Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] ≅ ⊕_{S relevant} IC_{S̄}(L_S), L_S := (R^{2d_S}f_*ℚ̄_ℓ)|_S, where L_S is the lisse sheaf whose geometric fibre at y is H^{2d_S}(f^{−1}(y)) ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ(−d_S)^{#(top-dimensional irreducible components of f^{−1}(y))}. The summand supported on S̄ (its S-isotypic part for the support decomposition) is canonically determined.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
X₀ smooth of pure dimension n; f₀ proper surjective and semismall; the stratification makes all R^q f_*ℚ̄_ℓ lisse on strata.
proofSteps: Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] is perverse by the smooth-source constant-coefficient semismall criterion (the special case stated in EDC.5/semismall-pushforward-perversity; de Cataldo–Migliorini Proposition 4.2.1), and pure of weight n by DWP.8/twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (c) and DWP.8/proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6.

By EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity, Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] = ⊕ IC_{S̄}(M_S) over 𝔽̄_q, grouping simple constituents by the stratum of the generic point of their support, with M_S semisimple lisse on S (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification).
Restrict to a stratum S: an IC_{S̄′}(M_{S′}) with S ⊂ S̄′ ∖ S′ has ℋ^j vanishing on S for j ≥ −dim S (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension stalk bound), so ℋ^{−dim S}(Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n])|_S = M_S.

By proper base change the left side is R^{n−dim S}f_*ℚ̄_ℓ|_S, whose fibres are H^{n−dim S}(f^{−1}(y)); semismallness gives n − dim S ≥ 2 d_S, so it vanishes unless S is relevant, where it is the top cohomology H^{2d_S}(f^{−1}(y)) = ℚ̄_ℓ(−d_S)^{#top components} (EDC.2:trace-purity/top-degree-compact-cohomology).
The support decomposition of a semisimple perverse sheaf is canonical (the S-part is the sum of all simple subobjects with generic support point in S).
acceptance: For the blow-up of 𝔸² at the origin (n = 2): strata 𝔸²∖{0} (d = 0, relevant) and {0} (d = 1, 0 + 2 = 2, relevant), giving ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ δ₀(−1), matching EDC.7/decomposition-theorem's acceptance example.
For a small map (all non-dense strata irrelevant) the formula reduces to Rf_*ℚ̄_ℓ[n] ≅ IC_Y(L) with L = f_*ℚ̄_ℓ on the dense stratum, agreeing with EDC.5/small-pushforward-intersection-complex.
For the Springer resolution of the nilpotent cone of SL₂ (n = 2), the strata are the regular orbit (d = 0) and the origin (d = 1, relevant), giving ℚ̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ δ₀(−1) as for the A₁ surface singularity.

nodes.title: Graded Lefschetz objects and primitive parts in an abelian category with a Tate twist
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian category with an additive autoequivalence M ↦ M(1) and powers M(n), n ∈ ℤ. A graded Lefschetz object (L, η) consists of objects L^i ∈ A for i ∈ ℤ, zero outside a finite interval, and morphisms η_i : L^i → L^{i+2}(1). For r ≥ 0 its iterate η^r : L^{i} → L^{i+2r}(r) is η_{i+2r−2}(r−1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ η_i(0), with the canonical identifications (a)(b) ≅ (a+b). (L, η) satisfies hard Lefschetz if η^r : L^{−r} → L^{r}(r) is an isomorphism for every r ≥ 0. Its primitive part in degree −r ≤ 0 is the kernel P^{−r} := ker(η^{r+1} : L^{−r} → L^{r+2}(r+1)), with its inclusion into L^{−r}.
hypotheses: A abelian; (1) an additive autoequivalence with chosen coherence isomorphisms (a)(b) ≅ (a + b); in the application A = Perv(Y₀, ℚ̄_ℓ) or Perv(Y, ℚ̄_ℓ) and (1) is the Tate twist.
proofSteps: The iterate is defined by induction on r, composing with the twisted η and the coherence isomorphisms; hard Lefschetz and primitive parts are defined from it with Mathlib's kernels.
Morphisms of graded Lefschetz objects are families of morphisms commuting with η; kernels of η-iterates are functorial for them.
acceptance: For A = finite-dimensional ℚ̄_ℓ-vector spaces with trivial twist, L^i = H^{n+i}(X) of a smooth projective n-dimensional X and η = cup product with an ample class, this is the data of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/lefschetz-operator, and P^{−r} is the primitive cohomology P^{n−r}.

nodes.title: Primitive decomposition of a graded Lefschetz object satisfying hard Lefschetz
nodes.statement: Let (L, η) be a graded Lefschetz object in an abelian category with Tate twist (EDC.7/graded-lefschetz-object) satisfying hard Lefschetz. Then for every r ≥ 0 the map ⊕_{a ≥ 0} P^{−r−2a}(−a) → L^{−r}, given on the a-th summand by η^a composed with the primitive inclusion and the twist coherence, is an isomorphism (a finite biproduct), and for every r ≥ 0, L^{r} ≅ L^{−r}(−r) via η^r. Equivalently, in each degree n the map from the biproduct of the primitive string columns P^{−r}(−a), 0 ≤ a ≤ r, −r + 2a = n, to L^n is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Hard Lefschetz for all r ≥ 0; L of finite support. No splitting is assumed: the summands are the actual kernels and the maps are actual η-powers.
proofSteps: For r ≥ 0, η : L^{−r−2} → L^{−r}(1) is a monomorphism, since η^{r+1} ∘ η = η^{r+2} is an isomorphism on L^{−r−2}.
The endomorphism p := η ∘ (η^{r+2})^{−1}(−1) ∘ η^{r+1} of L^{−r} (with twists) is an idempotent with image η(L^{−r−2})(−1) and kernel P^{−r}; hence L^{−r} = P^{−r} ⊕ η L^{−r−2}(−1).
Iterate (induction on the length of the support) to obtain the full string decomposition; positive degrees follow from the isomorphisms η^r.
acceptance: In the vector-space case the statement is DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/lefschetz-decomposition-of-a-graded-operator (i)–(ii), including dim P^{n−r} = dim V^{n−r} − dim V^{n−r−2}.

nodes.title: Perverse cohomology along the universal hyperplane section
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y factor as a closed immersion X ↪ ℙ^d × Y followed by the projection, with η = c₁(𝒪(1)). Let Y′ = ℙ^{d∨} × Y, X′ = ℙ^{d∨} × X with u : X′ → X and u : Y′ → Y the projections (smooth of relative dimension d with connected fibres), H ⊂ X′ the universal hyperplane section, v : H ↪ X′ and h : H → Y′ the induced proper map. For K ∈ pD^{≥0}(X): (i) u^*Rf_*K ≅ Rf′_*u^*K, hence (u^*pH^i Rf_*K)[d] ≅ pH^{i+d}(Rf′_*u^*K); (ii) for i < d − 1, pH^i(Rf′_*u^*K) ≅ pH^i(Rh_*(uv)^*K); (iii) pH^{d−1}(Rf′_*u^*K) → pH^{d−1}(Rh_*(uv)^*K) is injective and identifies the source with the largest perverse subsheaf of the target that comes from Y (is of the form u^*G[d]).
hypotheses: X, Y separated of finite type over a field k (k = 𝔽_q or 𝔽̄_q), coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ; the factorisation through ℙ^d × Y is available locally on Y after replacing η by a multiple.
proofSteps: u is smooth of relative dimension d with connected fibres, so u^*[d] is t-exact and fully faithful on perverse sheaves, with a largest subobject and a largest quotient coming from Y (EDC.5/smooth-pullback-perverse-exactness, BBD 4.2.4–4.2.6); smooth base change gives (i).

u^*K lies in pD^{≥d}(X′); the projection g : U := X′ ∖ H → Y′ is affine, so g_!(u^*K|_U) ∈ pD^{≥d}(Y′) by left t-exactness of g_! (EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing, BBD 4.1.2); the triangle (g_!(u^*K|_U), Rf′_*u^*K, Rh_*(uv)^*K) gives (ii) and the injectivity in (iii).

For (iii) it remains to compare pH^{−d}u_* of the two sides; by the projective-bundle formula (EDC.4/projective-bundle-decomposition, BBD 5.4.12) u_*u^* = ⊕_{i=0}^{d} (−)[−2i](−i) and (uv)_*(uv)^* has the same summands for i ≤ d − 1, and the fibre-dimension bound gives the needed vanishing (BBD 5.4.13).
acceptance: For Y a point and X = ℙ^d itself, H is the universal hyperplane (incidence variety) and (ii)–(iii) recover the weak Lefschetz statement for hyperplane sections of ℙ^d in degrees below d − 1.

nodes.title: Relative hard Lefschetz
nodes.statement: Let f₀ : X₀ → Y₀ be a projective morphism of separated schemes of finite type over 𝔽_q and η ∈ H²(X₀, ℚ̄_ℓ(1)) the first Chern class of an f₀-ample line bundle. Cup product with η gives η : K₀ → K₀[2](1) for every K₀, hence η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*K₀) → pH^{i}(Rf₀_*K₀)(i). If F₀ is a pure perverse sheaf on X₀ of weight w, then for every i ≥ 0, η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) → pH^{i}(Rf₀_*F₀)(i) is an isomorphism of pure perverse sheaves of weight w − i on Y₀ (the same then holds over 𝔽̄_q). A proper morphism has no automatic ample class: projectivity and the chosen relatively ample line bundle are hypotheses.
hypotheses: X₀ separated of finite type over 𝔽_q (q a power of p), X := X₀ ⊗_{𝔽_q} 𝔽̄_q, ℓ ≠ p; coefficients ℚ̄_ℓ, realised as the 2-colimit of the rational adic categories D^b_c(−, E) over finite E/ℚ_ℓ (EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories, EDC.6/rational-perverse-coefficient-extension); 'perverse' refers to the middle perversity of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure with its ℓ-adic form EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures; mixed complexes and integer weights are those of DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/mixed-complexes and DWP.8/pure-complexes (a sheaf of weights ≤ w has ℋ^i of punctual weights ≤ w + i; weights ≥ w are defined by duality).
f₀ projective; the line bundle is f₀-ample; η is its Chern class in the adic theory (EDC.3/chern-classes, EDC.6/adic-transport-of-duality-and-classes); F₀ pure perverse.
proofSteps: The question is local on Y₀; after shrinking Y₀ and replacing η by a positive multiple (which does not change bijectivity of η^i), f₀ factors through ℙ^d × Y₀ with η = c₁(𝒪(1)).
Case i = 1: η is the composite of restriction pH^{−1}(Rf_*F) → pH^0(Rh_*((uv)^*F[d−1])) along the universal hyperplane and its dual Gysin map back to pH^1(Rf_*F)(1) (after u^*[d]).
By EDC.7/universal-hyperplane-lemma, u^*pH^{−1} is the largest subobject of P := pH^0(Rh_*((uv)^*F[d−1])) coming from Y, and dually u^*pH^1(1) is its largest quotient coming from Y.

(uv)^*F₀[d−1] is pure (smooth pullback), so Rh_* of it and P are pure (DWP.8/proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6, EDC.7/perverse-cohomology-weights), hence P is semisimple over 𝔽̄_q (EDC.7/pure-perverse-geometric-semisimplicity); the largest sub coming from Y maps isomorphically to the largest such quotient, so η is an isomorphism (BBD 5.4.14).
General i: induction on i, factoring u^*[d] of η^{i+1} through pH^{−i}h_*, the inductive isomorphism for h and (uv)^*F[d−1], and the dual Gysin map (BBD 5.4.15).
Weights: pH^{−i} has weight w − i and pH^{i}(i) has weight w + i − 2i = w − i.
acceptance: For Y₀ = Spec 𝔽_q, X₀ smooth projective of dimension n and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[n], the statement is DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/hard-lefschetz-4-1-1: η^i : H^{n−i}(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ H^{n+i}(X, ℚ̄_ℓ(i)).
For f₀ = ℙ¹ × Y₀ → Y₀ and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1 + dim Y₀] with Y₀ smooth: pH^{−1} = ℚ̄_ℓ[dim Y₀] and pH^{1} = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[dim Y₀], and η is the isomorphism given by the class of a point in H²(ℙ¹).

The ampleness hypothesis matters: for f : ℙ¹_{𝔽_q} → Spec 𝔽_q and F₀ = ℚ̄_ℓ[1], the trivial line bundle gives η = 0, so η¹ : pH^{−1} = H⁰(ℙ¹) → pH¹(1) = H²(ℙ¹)(1) is zero although both sides are ℚ̄_ℓ.

nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem, put P^{−i} := ker(η^{i+1} : pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) → pH^{i+2}(Rf₀_*F₀)(i+1)) for i ≥ 0. Then for every i ≥ 0, pH^{−i}(Rf₀_*F₀) ≅ ⊕_{a ≥ 0} P^{−i−2a}(−a) via η-powers, in Perv(Y₀); and over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*F ≅ ⊕_{i ≥ 0} ⊕_{a=0}^{i} P^{−i}(−a)[i − 2a] (non-canonically for the sum over degrees, by EDC.7/decomposition-theorem). Combine with the geometric splitting of EDC.7/decomposition-theorem (b) for the statement on Rf_*F; purity of P^{−i} by EDC.7/subquotient-weight-stability.

nodes.title: Hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be projective over 𝔽_q of pure dimension n, η the Chern class of an ample line bundle, and L₀ a lisse sheaf on a smooth dense open of X₀, punctually pure of weight w. Then for every i ≥ 0, cup product with η^i is an isomorphism IH^{n−i}(X, L) → IH^{n+i}(X, L)(i), where IH^j(X, L) := H^{j−n}(X, IC_X(L)), between spaces pure of weight w + n − i.

nodes.title: Restricted constructible categories and their specialisation to finite fields
nodes.statement: Let X be of finite type over ℂ, T a finite stratification of X into smooth connected algebraic strata and, for each T ∈ T, L(T) a finite set of isomorphism classes of irreducible locally constant sheaves of ℤ/ℓ-modules on T. D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) is the full subcategory of D^b_c(X, ℤ_ℓ) of objects whose cohomology sheaves, reduced mod ℓ and restricted to each stratum T, are locally constant with all constituents in L(T). Choose a finitely generated ℤ-subalgebra A ⊂ ℂ, S = Spec A, and a model (X_S, T_S, L_S) over S, shrunk so that strata are smooth over S with geometrically connected fibres and the Ext sheaves between the j_!L are locally constant and commute with base change. For a strictly henselian DVR V with A ⊂ V ⊂ ℂ whose residue field s̄ is an algebraic closure of a finite residue field of A, the restriction functors D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) ← D^b_{T,L}(X_V, ℤ_ℓ) → D^b_{T,L}(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ) are equivalences; the induced system of equivalences D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) ≃ D^b_{T,L}(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ), as a germ along the filter of such V, depends only on (X, T, L). After refining (T, L) and shrinking S, the equivalences respect any given finite list of the operations Rf_*, Rf_!, f^*, Rf^!, ⊗, RHom, the perverse t-structure (when the R^q j_*L|_{T′} are lisse with constituents in L(T′)), and rank, lissity and monodromy of sheaves on strata; they extend to ℚ_ℓ, E_λ and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients. There is no equivalence of the full categories D^b_c(X, ℤ_ℓ) ≃ D^b_c(X_s̄, ℤ_ℓ).
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
Only finitely many operations and objects are transported at a time; refinements change the germ only by restriction.
proofSteps: For ℤ/ℓⁿ coefficients the equivalences are formal from the identification of the H^p(−, Ext^q(F, G)) on X, X_V and X_s̄ for F, G of the form j_!L (smooth and proper base change on the chosen model, generic base change, SF.2 spreading out) (BBD 6.1.9).

Finite Tor dimension is preserved, and the ℓ-adic statement follows from the definition of ℓ-adic derived categories as normalized systems (EDC.6/normalized-adic-system, EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories).

Compatibility with operations and with the perverse t-structure: enlarge (T, L) so that the operations send the restricted categories into restricted categories, then shrink S so that base change holds (BBD 6.1.10, using EGA IV §§8–9 spreading-out lists, 6.1.7).
Over ℂ, the étale category is compared with the analytic one by EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison.
acceptance: For X = a point and T = {X}, D^b_{T,L}(X, ℤ_ℓ) is the category of perfect ℤ_ℓ-complexes, identical over ℂ and over s̄; for X = ℙ¹_ℂ with one stratum and L = {ℤ/ℓ}, the specialisation sends Rπ_*ℤ_ℓ to Rπ_*ℤ_ℓ on ℙ¹_{s̄}, both with cohomology ℤ_ℓ, 0, ℤ_ℓ(−1).

On X = 𝔾_{m,ℂ} the ℤ_ℓ-local system with monodromy a non-quasi-unipotent element of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ) is not in any D_{T,L} coming from a model over a finitely generated A, illustrating why only restricted categories specialise (BBD 6.1.8).

nodes.title: Perverse sheaves and complexes of geometric origin
nodes.statement: For schemes X of finite type over ℂ, the class of simple perverse sheaves of complex vector spaces of geometric origin is the smallest class (a) containing the constant sheaf ℂ on a point and (b) closed under taking the simple constituents of pH^i T(F) for T one of Rf_*, Rf_!, f^*, Rf^! (f a morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ), and (c) closed under taking the simple constituents of pH^i(A ⊗ B) and pH^i RHom(A, B) for A, B with constituents in the class. A perverse sheaf is semisimple of geometric origin if it is a finite direct sum of simple ones of geometric origin; a complex K ∈ D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) is semisimple of geometric origin if K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(K)[−i] and each pH^i(K) is semisimple of geometric origin.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
The definition is inductive over all schemes of finite type over ℂ; constituents are simple subquotients in the analytic perverse heart.
proofSteps: The class exists as the intersection of all classes with properties (a)–(c).
The full subcategories of D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) of objects whose perverse cohomology constituents are of geometric origin are stable under f_*, f_!, f^*, f^!, ⊗ and RHom by construction (BBD 6.2.4).
acceptance: For j : U ↪ X an open immersion with U smooth connected of dimension d and L a local system with finite monodromy on U, j_!*(L[d]) is semisimple of geometric origin, since L is a direct summand of π_*ℂ for a finite étale cover π.

nodes.title: Simple perverse sheaves of geometric origin specialise to pure sheaves over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let F be a simple perverse ℚ̄_ℓ-sheaf of geometric origin on X over ℂ (transported from ℂ to ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients by a field isomorphism and EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison). For S = Spec A, A ⊂ ℂ finitely generated over ℤ and large enough, each specialisation equivalence of EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories sends F to a simple perverse sheaf F_s̄ on X_s̄ satisfying (P): X_s̄ comes by extension of scalars from some X₀ over a finite field 𝔽_q and F_s̄ from a pure perverse sheaf F₀ on X₀.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
The model, the finite field and the pure F₀ are part of the output (a witness), not assumptions; purity is a conclusion.
proofSteps: Simplicity is preserved by the specialisation equivalences (EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories, perverse t-exactness).

By the inductive definition (EDC.7/geometric-origin-class) it suffices that (P) holds for ℚ̄_ℓ on a point and is stable under the generating operations, which commute with the equivalences after refining and shrinking.

If F_s̄, G_s̄ satisfy (P), then pH^iT(F₀) (and pH^i of ⊗, RHom) are mixed (EDC.7/mixed-perverse-sheaves, DWP.8/six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11); their simple constituents are pure (EDC.7/simple-mixed-perverse-is-pure) and, by EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories, the constituents of the specialised objects are their pullbacks (BBD 6.2.6).
acceptance: For F = ℂ_X[d] with X smooth over ℂ, F₀ can be taken to be ℚ̄_ℓ[d] on a smooth model X₀, pure of weight d.

sources.match: BBD prove that, for S large, the specialisation equivalences send a simple perverse sheaf of geometric origin to a simple perverse sheaf coming from a pure one over a finite field, by stability of property (P) under the generating operations.

nodes.title: The decomposition theorem over ℂ
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ. If K ∈ D^b_c(X(ℂ), ℂ) is semisimple of geometric origin, then Rf_*K is semisimple of geometric origin: Rf_*K ≅ ⊕_i pH^i(Rf_*K)[−i] and each pH^i(Rf_*K) is a finite direct sum of simple perverse sheaves of geometric origin. The same holds with ℂ replaced by ℚ̄_ℓ in the étale topology. In particular, for X smooth (resp. any X and L of geometric origin), Rf_*ℂ_X[dim X] (resp. Rf_*IC_X(L)) decomposes in this way. No ℚ- or ℚ_ℓ-rational descent of the splitting is asserted.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
K semisimple of geometric origin; complex (or ℚ̄_ℓ) coefficients.
proofSteps: Reduce to K = F simple perverse of geometric origin (finite sums and shifts).

Choose S large and specialise (EDC.7/pure-specialization-of-geometric-origin): F_s̄ comes from a pure F₀ on X₀ over 𝔽_q, and f, refined (T, L) on Y and the operation Rf_* are compatible with the equivalences (EDC.7/restricted-constructible-categories).

Over 𝔽̄_q, Rf_*F_s̄ splits as ⊕ pH^i[−i] with semisimple pH^i (EDC.7/decomposition-theorem); transport back through the equivalences to get the statement for Rf_*F; the constituents are of geometric origin by definition (BBD 6.2.7).
acceptance: For the blow-up π of ℂ² at 0, Rπ_*ℂ[2] ≅ ℂ[2] ⊕ ℂ_0 (the complex counterpart of the 𝔽_q example of EDC.7/decomposition-theorem).
For f : X → point with X projective, the theorem gives H*(X, IC_X) as a graded vector space, the content being the existence of the IC formalism rather than splitting.

sources.match: BBD: for proper f, Rf_* of a semisimple complex of geometric origin is semisimple of geometric origin, proved by specialising to a finite field and applying 5.4.5 and 5.3.8.

nodes.title: Relative hard Lefschetz over ℂ
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a projective morphism of schemes of finite type over ℂ, η the first Chern class of a relatively ample line bundle, and F a semisimple perverse sheaf of geometric origin on X. Then for every i ≥ 0, η^i : pH^{−i}(Rf_*F) → pH^{i}(Rf_*F) is an isomorphism (Tate twists trivialised by the choice of 2πi). For Y a point this is hard Lefschetz in intersection cohomology of complex projective varieties.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over ℂ; complex coefficients for the analytic statements and ℚ̄_ℓ coefficients for the étale ones, related by a chosen field isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ and by the étale/analytic comparison of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison; strata are algebraic.
f projective with a chosen relatively ample line bundle; F semisimple of geometric origin.
proofSteps: Specialise F to a pure F₀ over a finite field (EDC.7/pure-specialization-of-geometric-origin) with f and η compatible after shrinking S.
Apply EDC.7/relative-hard-lefschetz-theorem over 𝔽_q and transport back (BBD 6.2.10).
acceptance: For X smooth projective over ℂ and F = ℂ[dim X], Y a point: η^i : H^{n−i}(X, ℂ) ≅ H^{n+i}(X, ℂ), the classical hard Lefschetz theorem.

nodes.title: Correspondences of schemes and their morphisms
nodes.statement: A correspondence from X₁ to X₂ is a morphism c = (c₁, c₂) : C → X₁ × X₂ of schemes separated of finite type over k. A morphism from c : C → X₁ × X₂ to b : B → Y₁ × Y₂ is a triple [f] = (f₁, f♮, f₂) with b₁f♮ = f₁c₁ and b₂f♮ = f₂c₂. [f] is proper (resp. an open or closed embedding) when f₁, f♮ and f₂ are. A self-correspondence is c : C → X × X; its fixed-point scheme is Fix(c) := C ×_{X×X} X (fibre product with the diagonal Δ), with Δ′ : Fix(c) → C and c′ : Fix(c) → X. A compactification of c is a correspondence c̄ : C̄ → X̄₁ × X̄₂ proper over k with a dominant open embedding [j] : c → c̄; every pair of compactifications of X₁, X₂ extends to one of c.
hypotheses: Schemes separated of finite type over a field k; fibre products are the native scheme fibre products.
proofSteps: Composition of morphisms of correspondences is componentwise; Fix is functorial for morphisms of self-correspondences with f₁ = f₂.
Existence of compactifications: compactify C by Nagata and take the closure of C in C′ × X̄₁ × X̄₂ (Varshavsky 1.1.3).
acceptance: The graph-type correspondence (g, id) : X → X × X of an endomorphism g has Fix equal to the fixed-point scheme X^g.
The transpose c^t = (c₂, c₁) has Fix(c^t) ≅ Fix(c).

nodes.title: Cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: Let c : C → X₁ × X₂ be a correspondence, F₁ ∈ D^b_ctf(X₁, Λ) and F₂ ∈ D^b_ctf(X₂, Λ). A cohomological correspondence lifting c (a c-morphism) from F₁ to F₂ is a morphism u : c₁^*F₁ → c₂^!F₂ in D(C, Λ); equivalently, by the adjunction c₂_! ⊣ c₂^!, a morphism c₂_!c₁^*F₁ → F₂. Hom_c(F₁, F₂) := Hom(c₁^*F₁, c₂^!F₂). Convention: pull back along the first leg and apply the exceptional inverse image along the second; the stage description's c₂^*K → c₁^!K is the same notion with the legs named in the opposite order. For an endomorphism g : X → X, the graph-type correspondence is (g, id) : X → X × X (c₁ = g, c₂ = id), whose c-morphisms are the maps u : g^*F → F.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
proofSteps: The adjunction c₂_! ⊣ c₂^! is EDC.1:adjoint/exceptional-inverse-image; it identifies the two descriptions naturally in F₁, F₂.
For c the identity correspondence of X, Hom_c(F₁, F₂) = Hom(F₁, F₂) (since id^! = id).
acceptance: For c = (g, id) the graph-type correspondence of an endomorphism g, a c-morphism is a map u : g^*F → F; for g the Frobenius of X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, the Weil structure Fr^*F ≅ F of a sheaf on X₀ is one.
For X₁ = X₂ = C = Spec k, a c-morphism is a morphism of perfect Λ-complexes F₁ → F₂.

nodes.statement: Let [f] = (f₁, f♮, f₂) : c → b be a morphism of correspondences satisfying one of: (i) the square (c₁, f♮, f₁, b₁) is cartesian; (ii) f₁ and f♮ are proper; (iii) c₁ and b₁ are proper. nodes.title: Pullback, open restriction and restriction to invariant closed subsets
nodes.statement: (a) Pullback: if [f] : c → b has its right square cartesian up to nilpotents, or f♮ and f₂ étale, there is BC : c₂_!f♮^* → f₂^*b₂_!, and a b-morphism u gives a c-morphism [f]^*(u) : c₂_!c₁^*(f₁^*F₁) → f₂^*F₂. (b) Open restriction: for a self-correspondence c and open W ⊂ C, U ⊂ X, u restricts to u|_W and to u|_U on c|_U : c₁^{−1}(U) ∩ c₂^{−1}(U) → U × U. (c) A closed Z ⊂ X is c-invariant if c₁(c₂^{−1}(Z)) ⊂ Z set-theoretically, and locally c-invariant if each z ∈ Z has an open neighbourhood U with Z ∩ U c|_U-invariant; for c-invariant Z, c|_Z : c₂^{−1}(Z)_red → Z × Z and u restricts to u|_Z; in general one first restricts to the largest open W(Z) ⊂ C over which Z is invariant. (d) If c₂ is quasi-finite and x is a closed point, Fix(c|_x) is finite and for y ∈ Fix(c|_x) the restriction u_y : F_x → F_x is the summand of (c₂_!c₁^*F)_x → F_x at y; Tr(u_y) is the naive local term.
hypotheses: All schemes are separated of finite type over a field k (separably closed whenever trace maps, local terms or traces on cohomology occur); ℓ is invertible in k; Λ is a finite ring killed by a power of ℓ, or a finite extension of ℤ_ℓ or ℚ_ℓ (in the adic case D^b_ctf is the category of EDC.6/classical-and-proetale-adic-categories); D^b_ctf(X, Λ) is the category of constructible complexes of finite Tor dimension (EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes), stable under the six operations.
proofSteps: (a), (b): base change for cartesian squares up to nilpotents (topological invariance, SF.2) and étale base change (Varshavsky 1.1.8–1.1.9).

(c): the largest open W(Z) is the complement of the closure of c₂^{−1}(Z) ∖ c₁^{−1}(Z) (Varshavsky Lemma 1.5.3(b)); invariance makes the inclusion of c|_Z cartesian up to nilpotents, so (a) applies (1.5.6).
(d): for quasi-finite c₂ the stalk (c₂_!c₁^*F)_x is the direct sum of the stalks of c₁^*F over c₂^{−1}(x) (Varshavsky 1.5.7).
acceptance: For c the graph-type correspondence of an automorphism g with g(Z) = Z, Z is c-invariant and u|_Z is the restricted equivariant structure on F|_Z.
Example 1.5.2 of Varshavsky: a closed point x with c₂^{−1}(x) finite is locally c-invariant.
